name: OpenFDA_search_drug_labels
description: Search the FDA drug label (SPL - Structured Product Labeling) database via openFDA. Contains approved prescription and OTC drug labels including indications, warnings, dosage, adverse reactions, contraindications, and pharmacology sections. Use Lucene query syntax: 'openfda.brand_name:aspirin', 'openfda.generic_name:ibuprofen', 'openfda.manufacturer_name:pfizer'. Returns label text sections and openFDA cross-references (brand name, generic name, substance name, product type). Some labels are not linked to openFDA fields (for example TAGRISSO / osimertinib), so an 'openfda.*' query can find nothing even though the label exists: search the name as free text ('TAGRISSO'), or use FDA_search_drug_labels with drug_name, which also checks unlinked labels. Exact totals and skip pagination: continue with metadata.next_skip while metadata.has_more is true; metadata discloses openFDA's 25,100-record reachable window for very broad searches.

search.description: Lucene query to search drug labels (e.g., 'openfda.brand_name:aspirin', 'openfda.generic_name:metformin', 'indications_and_usage:diabetes', 'openfda.pharm_class_epc:"beta blocker"')

skip.description: Number of matching records to skip. Continue with metadata.next_skip.

fields.unreachable_alternatives: If this was a 'no matches' answer to an openfda.* query, the label may still exist without openFDA fields (for example TAGRISSO / osimertinib): retry with the name as free text, for example search='TAGRISSO', or use FDA_search_drug_labels with drug_name.

name: OpenFDA_search_drug_events
description: Search the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database via openFDA for drug safety reports. Accepts convenience parameters drug_name and reaction (e.g., drug_name='warfarin', reaction='haemorrhage'), a raw Lucene 'search' string for advanced queries, or any combination of them -- whichever you supply are AND-ed together, so passing 'search' alongside drug_name narrows that drug rather than replacing it. Contains 20+ million adverse event reports. IMPORTANT: MedDRA reaction terms use British English spelling (e.g., 'haemorrhage' not 'hemorrhage', 'haematoma' not 'hematoma'). Returns serious adverse events with outcomes (hospitalization, death), suspect drugs, and MedDRA reactions. Record mode exposes exact totals and skip pagination; continue with metadata.next_skip. Count mode does not support skip and reports whether its term list reached the requested limit.

search.description: Lucene query for adverse event reports. Use AND/OR with spaces (not +AND+). A FAERS report names its drug in up to three fields and none is a superset of the others, so a drug clause must OR all three inside parentheses or it undercounts (measured 2026-08-11: tofacitinib has 13,075 reports under patient.drug.medicinalproduct alone against 186,783 across all three). Prefer the 'drug_name' parameter, which builds that clause for you. Examples: '(patient.drug.medicinalproduct:aspirin OR patient.drug.openfda.generic_name:aspirin OR patient.drug.openfda.brand_name:aspirin)', 'patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt:"myocardial infarction"', 'serious:1 AND (patient.drug.medicinalproduct:warfarin OR patient.drug.openfda.generic_name:warfarin OR patient.drug.openfda.brand_name:warfarin)'. Combine drugs by AND-ing one parenthesized group per drug.

limit.description: Record mode: max 100. Count mode: max 1000 terms.

count.description: Field to count by for frequency analysis (e.g., 'patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact' to get most common reactions)

drug_name.description: Drug name to search for adverse events (e.g., 'warfarin', 'metformin'). Brand or generic: the name is matched against patient.drug.medicinalproduct, patient.drug.openfda.generic_name and patient.drug.openfda.brand_name, the same three fields every FAERS_* tool searches. Alternative to writing a full Lucene 'search' query, and preferred over it.

reaction.description: MedDRA adverse reaction term (British spelling: 'haemorrhage' not 'hemorrhage', 'haematoma' not 'hematoma'). Used with drug_name to filter by reaction.

adverse_event.description: Alias for reaction. MedDRA adverse reaction term (British spelling).

skip.description: Record mode only. Number of reports to skip; continue with metadata.next_skip. Must be 0 when count is used.

disclaimer.description: openFDA's standing disclaimer: the data is not for making decisions about medical care. It is returned on every response and belongs in the answer rather than being silently dropped.

license.description: Licence URL for the data, https://open.fda.gov/license/.

actiondrug.description: What was done with the drug: '1' withdrawn, '2' dose reduced, '3' dose increased, '4' dose not changed, '5' unknown, '6' not applicable. Dechallenge is one of the strongest causality signals and this is where it is recorded.

activesubstance.description: The active substance as reported, with its name.

drugadministrationroute.description: Route code for how the drug was given.

drugauthorizationnumb.description: The drug's marketing authorisation number, e.g. '050007'.

drugdosageform.description: Dosage form as the reporter wrote it.

drugdosagetext.description: Dose as free text, e.g. 'UNK' when unknown.

drugindication.description: What the drug was given for, as a MedDRA term. Distinguishes an adverse reaction from the condition being treated.

drugrecurreadministration.description: Whether the reaction returned on re-exposure: '1' yes, '2' no, '3' unknown. Rechallenge is the other causality signal.

drugstartdate.description: When the drug was started, as the format in drugstartdateformat.

drugstructuredosagenumb.description: Dose as a number, when the reporter gave a structured one.

openfda.description: openFDA's resolved identifiers for the reported drug - application_number, brand_name, generic_name, rxcui, unii and the pharmacologic classes. Empty when openFDA could not resolve the reported name, which is common in FAERS.

reactionmeddrapt.description: MedDRA preferred term for the adverse reaction

reactionmeddraversionpt.description: MedDRA version the reaction term was coded against, e.g. '17.0'. Terms change between versions, so comparing counts across versions needs this.

patientagegroup.description: Age group code: '1' neonate, '2' infant, '3' child, '4' adolescent, '5' adult, '6' elderly.

patientonsetage.description: Patient's age at onset, as a number whose UNIT is in patientonsetageunit - the two must be read together.

patientonsetageunit.description: Unit for patientonsetage: '800' decade, '801' year, '802' month, '803' week, '804' day, '805' hour.

patientsex.description: Patient sex code: '1' male, '2' female. A bare digit, so it is unusable without this.

companynumb.description: The reporting company's own case number, e.g. 'US-PFIZER INC-2014063856'. What links a case across the versions a company files.

duplicate.description: '1' when FDA has flagged the report as a duplicate of another. Counting duplicates as separate events inflates every FAERS tally.

fulfillexpeditecriteria.description: '1' when the case met FDA's expedited-reporting criteria - that is, serious and unexpected. '2' when it did not.

occurcountry.description: Country the event occurred in, which can differ from where it was reported.

primarysource.description: The original reporter: their country and `qualification` (1 physician, 2 pharmacist, 3 other health professional, 4 lawyer, 5 consumer). A consumer report and a physician report are not equal evidence.

primarysourcecountry.description: Country the report came from, as a two-letter code.

receiptdate.description: When FDA received the most recent version, YYYYMMDD. With receivedate this shows how long a case has been revised.

receiptdateformat.description: Format code for receiptdate; '102' is YYYYMMDD.

receivedate.description: When FDA first received the case, YYYYMMDD.

receivedateformat.description: Format code for receivedate; '102' is YYYYMMDD. Present because FAERS does not guarantee one format.

receiver.description: Who received it, with type and organisation.

reportduplicate.description: Which report this duplicates, with the source and that source's case number.

reporttype.description: FAERS report type code: '1' spontaneous, '2' report from study, '3' other, '4' not available to sender.

safetyreportversion.description: Version of this safety report, e.g. '2'. Later versions supersede earlier ones, and counting both double-counts the case.

sender.description: Who sent the report to FDA, with type and organisation.

transmissiondate.description: When the record was transmitted, YYYYMMDD.

transmissiondateformat.description: Format code for transmissiondate; '102' is YYYYMMDD.

spl_id.description: Id of the SPL document this listing came from. Joins the NDC directory to the label endpoints.

name: OpenFDA_search_drug_shortages
description: Search the FDA drug shortages database via openFDA (added 2025). Returns current and resolved U.S. drug shortages with generic name, dosage form, presentation, shortage status (Current/Resolved), reported reason for the shortage, therapeutic category, manufacturer, and availability/related info. Use for supply-chain monitoring, formulary planning, and identifying alternatives for drugs in shortage. NOT a substitute for the official FDA shortage list for clinical decisions.

search.description: Lucene query for drug shortages (e.g., 'status:Current', 'generic_name:amoxicillin', 'dosage_form:Injection', 'therapeutic_category:Antibiotic'). Combine with AND/OR.

skip.description: Number of results to skip; continue with metadata.next_skip (max 25000)

availability.description: The product's current availability, e.g. 'Available'. The answer a shortage question is asking for.

contact_info.description: Phone number for the manufacturer's supply contact.

openfda.description: openFDA's resolved identifiers for the product: application_number, brand_name, generic_name, manufacturer_name and the rest. How a shortage joins to the label and NDC endpoints.

package_ndc.description: Package-level NDC of the affected presentation, e.g. '63323-488-17'. A shortage applies to a package, not to a drug in general.

related_info.description: FDA's note on what to do, e.g. 'Check wholesalers for inventory'.

update_type.description: What kind of update this record is, e.g. 'Reverified', 'Revised'. A reverified entry is a confirmation, not a new shortage.

Use for device safety signal detection and post-market surveillance. MAUDE reports are unverified and do not establish causation.

mdr_report_key.description: FDA's key for the MDR report, e.g. '10000007'. The report's identity.

mfr_report_type.description: The manufacturer's reporting obligation, e.g. 'Thirty-Day', 'Five-Day'. Five-Day means FDA judged it urgent.

noe_summarized.description: How many events the record summarises, when summary_report_flag is set.

number_devices_in_event.description: How many devices were involved. Empty when not reported.

number_patients_in_event.description: How many patients were involved. Empty when not reported.

pma_pmn_number.description: The PMA or 510(k) number the device was cleared under, e.g. 'P930039'. The join to the approval record.

previous_use_code.description: Whether the device had been used before, as openFDA's code.

product_problems.description: What went wrong with the device, e.g. ['Under-Sensing']. The substance of an adverse-event report and it was undeclared.

remedial_action.description: What was done about it, e.g. ['Recall'], ['Notification'].

removal_correction_number.description: FDA number of the removal or correction action, when one was taken.

report_source_code.description: Who the report came from, e.g. 'Manufacturer report', 'Voluntary report'. A manufacturer report and a voluntary one are not equal evidence.

report_to_fda.description: Whether the event was reported to FDA. '*' means openFDA has no value, not 'no'.

report_to_manufacturer.description: Whether the event was reported to the manufacturer.

reporter_country_code.description: One component of a postal address or telephone number openFDA splits across many keys (manufacturer, manufacturer contact, manufacturer G1 and distributor each have their own set). Populated on some reports and empty on most. Declared because the field exists, not because it carries the event.

reporter_state_code.description: One component of a postal address or telephone number openFDA splits across many keys (manufacturer, manufacturer contact, manufacturer G1 and distributor each have their own set). Populated on some reports and empty on most. Declared because the field exists, not because it carries the event.

reprocessed_and_reused_flag.description: 'Y' when a single-use device was reprocessed and reused - which is itself a contributing factor.

single_use_flag.description: Whether the device is labelled single-use.

summary_report_flag.description: 'Y' when the record summarises many events rather than describing one. A summary report counted as one event undercounts badly.

suppl_dates_mfr_received.description: Dates the manufacturer received supplemental information.

type_of_report.description: Report stage, e.g. ['Initial submission'], ['Follow-up']. A follow-up revises an earlier report rather than adding an event.

name: OpenFDA_search_device_recalls
description: Search the FDA medical-device recall database via openFDA. Returns device recalls with product description, recalling firm, recall status, FDA-determined cause, classification, associated 510(k)/PMA numbers, product code, and key dates (initiated/posted/terminated). Use for device safety research and tracking corrective actions. Distinct from device enforcement reports.

skip.description: Number of results to skip; continue with metadata.next_skip (max 25000)

action.description: What the firm actually did, e.g. the recall notice it issued and when.

code_info.description: Lot or serial numbers covered by the recall. The only field that says whether a particular unit is affected.

distribution_pattern.description: Where the product went, e.g. 'Worldwide Distribution -- USA, Canada, Hong Kong...'. Whether a recall reaches a given market depends on this.

event_date_terminated.description: When FDA closed the recall event, YYYY-MM-DD. An open recall and a closed one are different facts.

firm_fei_number.description: FDA establishment identifier of the recalling firm.

openfda.description: openFDA's resolved identifiers for the device: k_number, registration_number, fei_number, device_name, medical_specialty_description and regulation_number. The join to the 510(k), classification and adverse-event endpoints.

product_quantity.description: How much product was affected, e.g. '2246 units'.

reason_for_recall.description: Why the device was recalled, in FDA's words - e.g. 'Failure-- product can kink or ovalize, which may result in difficulty...'. The substance of a recall record and it was undeclared.

res_event_number.description: FDA's recall event number, e.g. '53426'. Joins the records of one event together.

root_cause_description.description: FDA's root-cause category, e.g. 'Device Design'. What separates a manufacturing lapse from a design flaw.

name: OpenFDA_search_food_adverse_events
description: Search the FDA CAERS database (Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition Adverse Event Reporting System) via openFDA. Covers adverse events and product complaints for foods, dietary supplements, and cosmetics. Returns reported reactions (MedDRA terms), patient outcomes, product role/industry, and dates. Use for supplement/cosmetic/food safety surveillance. Reports are voluntary, unverified, and do not establish causation.

search.description: Lucene query for CAERS food/supplement/cosmetic events (e.g., 'reactions:NAUSEA', 'products.industry_name:Cosmetics', 'outcomes:"Hospitalization"', 'products.role:Suspect').

skip.description: Number of results to skip; continue with metadata.next_skip (max 25000)

name: OpenFDA_search_animalvet_adverse_events
description: Search the FDA animal & veterinary adverse-event database via openFDA. Contains reports of adverse drug experiences in animals (and humans exposed) involving veterinary drugs. Returns affected animal species/breed, reactions (VeDDRA terms), drug(s) involved, number of animals affected/treated, outcome/health assessment, and dates. Use for veterinary pharmacovigilance. Reports are voluntary and do not establish causation.

skip.description: Number of results to skip; continue with metadata.next_skip (max 25000)

duration.description: How long the signs lasted, as a value and a unit.

foreign_or_domestic.description: Whether the report came from inside the US, e.g. 'Domestic'.

health_assessment_prior_to_exposure.description: The animal's condition before the drug, with who assessed it. The baseline the event has to be read against.

primary_reporter.description: Who reported it, e.g. 'Other Health Care Professional'. A veterinarian's report and an owner's report are not equal evidence.

receiver.description: The organisation that received the report, with its address.

report_id.description: FDA's identifier for the report, e.g. 'N141068'.

serious_ae.description: Whether the event was serious, as the string 'true' or 'false'. Not a boolean - openFDA sends it as text.

treated_for_ae.description: Whether the animal was treated for the event, as 'true' or 'false'.

type_of_information.description: What kind of report this is, e.g. 'Safety Issue', 'Lack of Effectiveness'.
